column4: The notification list navigates to an unvalidated URL taken straight from the notification payload
column5: getNotificationRedirectUrl at src/helpers/notificationUrl.ts:38-52 reads the first present value among redirect_url and url and link and target_url and target and returns it verbatim as quickLink with no scheme check and no same-origin check. The notifications page then navigates to it with a bare router.push - handleNavigate at src/pages/my-account/notifications/index.tsx:235-240 - so a payload carrying an absolute URL sends the customer to that origin in the SAME TAB carrying the storefront referrer. Every other branch of the helper builds a safe relative path such as /my-account/orders/{slug} - the quickLink shortcut is the only unvalidated one. Two counter-examples exist in the same codebase: safeNext at src/features/auth/safeNext.ts:8-11 validates the auth redirect by requiring a leading slash and rejecting a protocol relative form - and the push notification consumer at src/components/Functional/FirebaseInitializer.tsx:76-80 explicitly tests /^https?:\/\//i and opens an external URL through window.open with noopener and noreferrer instead of navigating in place. The notification list applies neither protection.

column11: A notification whose data carries a redirect_url or url or link or target field pointing off site.
column12: 1. Deliver a notification whose payload sets redirect_url to an external origin. 2. Open the notifications screen and click it. 3. Observe a same-tab navigation to that origin.
column13: An external target is either refused or opened deliberately in a new tab with noopener and noreferrer - matching what the push consumer already does.
column14: The customer is navigated off site in place with no interstitial and no indication they have left the storefront.
column15: A phishing path that begins inside an authenticated storefront screen - the customer clicks a notification they trust and lands on an attacker chosen page with the storefront as referrer. Credential prompts on the destination are far more convincing arriving this way.
column16: Validate quickLink before returning it - accept only a relative path as safeNext does - and if outbound notification links are a required feature route them through the same window.open with noopener and noreferrer that FirebaseInitializer already uses rather than router.push.

column4: The profile avatar accepts any file of any size and is the second unvalidated upload path in the app
column5: The avatar handler at src/pages/my-account/profile/index.tsx:189 stores whatever the picker returns with if (file) setProfileImageFile(file) - there is no mime check and no size check - and the file is appended to the profile submission at :210. The accept="image/*" attribute at :599 is a picker hint and not validation. This is the same class as CWEB-06 which records the return evidence upload and the two together describe the systemic position: the storefront has three upload paths and only one validates. src/components/Cart/AttachmentUploader.tsx:41-60 does it correctly with a size ceiling and a type allowlist - src/components/Modals/ReturnOrderItemModal.tsx:320 and :329 also did it correctly but that component is dead code - and the two live paths that replaced or bypassed them validate nothing.

column12: 1. Open the profile screen and choose the avatar picker. 2. Switch the dialog filter to all files and select a non-image and separately a very large file. 3. Save the profile and observe both are sent.
column13: Only images within a size ceiling are accepted - matching AttachmentUploader which already implements exactly this.
column14: Any file of any size is accepted and submitted as the profile image.
column15: Storage and bandwidth abuse on an authenticated endpoint - and a non-image accepted as an avatar is served back wherever the avatar renders which makes it a candidate injection vector under the same conditions described in CWEB-06.
column16: Apply the AttachmentUploader checks to the avatar picker - an image mime allowlist and a size ceiling with a message per rejected file. Better still extract those checks into one shared validator and route all three upload paths through it so a fourth cannot skip them.
